**Historian's answer on day 14**

**(1) Day-14 entries.** My source has one day-14 record, HIS-043. Its CSV row reads: "heldere dag", gebeurd_op "dag 14 11:35", vastgelegd_op "dag 14 11:35", onderwerp "weer". It records no leyline, shield, datanet or animal disturbance. No kroniek entry is headed dag 14. The nearest entries are HIS-111 (dag 13) and HIS-112 (dag 15), and neither concerns day 14 events. HIS-114 (dag 19) claims that the Burchtader stopped on the night of day 10, not day 14. That is my own unsupported speculation, not a day-14 record.

**(2) Day-14 leyline or pre-dawn readings.** My source contains no ARC-series records, so I cannot confirm or refute the Archmage's readings, including the Burchtader, Kloosterader, or any pre-dawn observation. The only pre-06:00 entries I hold are HIS-035 (dag 10 04:45), HIS-036 (dag 10 04:50), HIS-053 (dag 22 04:15) and HIS-054 (dag 22 05:00). None falls on day 14. HIS-106 (dag 6) states that in 23 years of datanet beside the leylines the register records no "hapering van de leylijnen". That covers only the period up to day 6, and it does not speak to day 14.

**(3) Datanet pacing on or before day 14.** Neither HIS-106 nor any other record in my source states that the datanet pacing changed on or before day 14. HIS-106 says nothing about pacing. "Op eigen maat" does not appear anywhere in my source, so I cannot verify ARC-106. The datanet entries I hold are HIS-005, HIS-006 and HIS-007 (construction and connection, 23 years earlier), HIS-014 (dag 3: woudkabels inspected, "niets gewijzigd"), HIS-026 (dag 7, leeslijst verstuurd), and HIS-036 (dag 10 complaint of half-arrived messages, vastgelegd dag 9 23:55). HIS-102 describes the datanet as running on the Kroonklok pols, but gives no pacing detail. The only pacing-related rule I hold is HIS-109 ("Een tweede pols ernaast brengt het uit de maat"), which is a design principle, not a record of a change.

**Integrity note.** HIS-036 breaches HIS-103 because its vastgelegd_op (dag 9 23:55) precedes its gebeurd_op (dag 10 04:50). This matters for any day-10 datanet timeline.
